## Services (BVA-derived 2026 price ranges)

### Hardwood Flooring — https://bvaflooring.com/hardwood-flooring/
Real wood rewards good installation and punishes shortcuts — especially in Florida. Engineered hardwood is the Gulf-Coast workhorse because its layered core shrugs off the humidity swings that make solid planks cup. Whichever you choose, the result lives or dies on acclimation, moisture testing, and a flat subfloor.
Pricing: Engineered hardwood — installed $9–$14 / sq ft; Solid / site-finished — installed $12–$18 / sq ft; Stair nosing & transitions $45–$90 / piece; Tear-out & haul-away $1.50–$3 / sq ft
Includes: Engineered & solid hardwood, Site-finished & prefinished options, Documented moisture testing, 48–72 hr acclimation, Precision jamb undercuts, Color-matched fill & putty, Stair nosing & transitions, Shoe molding reinstall

### Luxury Vinyl Plank — https://bvaflooring.com/vinyl-plank-flooring/
Waterproof, scratch-tough, and warm underfoot, luxury vinyl plank is the floor Florida homeowners and rental owners pick when they want wood looks without wood worries. The catch: rigid-core LVP telegraphs every bump in the subfloor. Flat-and-clean prep is the whole game.
Pricing: Floating LVP (5–6 mm) — installed $5–$8 / sq ft; Rigid-core SPC — installed $6–$9 / sq ft; Labor only (you supply material) $2.50–$4 / sq ft; Subfloor leveling $1–$3 / sq ft
Includes: Rigid-core SPC & floating LVP, 100% waterproof wear layers, Subfloor leveling & prep, Moisture barrier where needed, Tight, staggered seams, Square, sightline-true layout, Transitions & T-moldings, Quarter-round reinstall

### Tile Installation — https://bvaflooring.com/tile-installation/
Tile is the most permanent floor you can buy — which means a bad set is the most expensive to fix. Lippage, hollow spots, and crooked grout lines are all preventable with the right mortar coverage, layout, and a dead-flat base. We set tile to last decades, not seasons.
Pricing: Porcelain / ceramic floor — installed $9–$15 / sq ft; Large-format (24"+) — installed $13–$20 / sq ft; Shower / wet wall — installed $18–$28 / sq ft; Demo & prep $2–$4 / sq ft
Includes: Porcelain, ceramic & large-format, Showers, floors & lanais, Waterproofing at wet areas, Crack-isolation membrane, Back-buttered full coverage, Lippage-tuned, level sets, Even, sealed grout joints, Demo & subfloor prep

### Laminate Flooring — https://bvaflooring.com/laminate-flooring/
Modern laminate has come a long way — high-AC-rating planks look convincingly like wood and stand up to kids, pets, and traffic for a fraction of the cost. The difference between a floor that looks built-in and one that looks cheap is almost entirely in the seams and the prep.
Pricing: AC4 laminate — installed $4.50–$7 / sq ft; AC5 commercial-grade — installed $6–$8.50 / sq ft; Underlayment upgrade $0.40–$1 / sq ft; Labor only (you supply material) $2–$3.50 / sq ft
Includes: AC4 & AC5 commercial-grade, Wood, stone & tile looks, Quality underlayment, Subfloor flatten & clean, Tight, level seams, Expansion gaps held true, Transitions & reducers, Baseboard / shoe reinstall

### Stair Treads — https://bvaflooring.com/stair-treads/
Stairs are the hardest-working surface in the house and the most visible. Swapping tired carpet for solid wood treads transforms a staircase — but it is precision joinery, not plank-laying. Every tread has to be solid, quiet, and consistent, with overhangs and risers that line up.
Pricing: Retread over existing $80–$150 / tread; Full reface (tread + riser) $130–$220 / step; Carpet-to-wood conversion $140–$240 / step; Matching stain & seal $25–$50 / step
Includes: Carpet-to-wood conversions, Retreads over existing stairs, Solid & stained treads, Matching risers & nosing, Glued & mechanically fastened, Squeak elimination, Stain & seal to match floors, Quiet, code-minded rise/run

### Floor Repair & Replacement — https://bvaflooring.com/floor-repair/
Not every floor problem needs a full tear-out. Water-damaged boards, a few hollow tiles, an annoying squeak, or a failed seam can usually be fixed in place — if you catch it before it spreads. We diagnose honestly and fix the cause, not just the symptom.
Pricing: Diagnostic visit $95–$175; Board / plank replacement $8–$20 / sq ft; Hollow / cracked tile re-set $25–$55 / tile; Water-damage section $400–$1,400
Includes: Water-damaged board replacement, Hollow / cracked tile re-set, Squeak & movement fixes, Failed seam & gap repair, Transition & threshold fixes, Subfloor patch & flatten, Color & grain matching, Honest repair-vs-replace advice

### Hardwood Refinishing — https://bvaflooring.com/hardwood-refinishing/
Tired hardwood rarely needs replacing — it needs refinishing. Sanding back to raw wood, repairing gaps and damaged boards, and resealing brings a floor back to new for a fraction of replacement cost. The result lives or dies on dust control, even sanding, and choosing the right finish for Florida humidity.
Pricing: Sand & refinish — full $3.50–$6 / sq ft; Buff & coat (recoat) $1.50–$3 / sq ft; Board / plank repair $8–$20 / sq ft; Custom stain color change $0.75–$1.50 / sq ft
Includes: Dustless sand & refinish, Buff-and-coat / recoat option, Board & plank repair, Gap fill & squeak re-nailing, Custom stain color matching, Water-based & oil finishes, Edge & corner detail sanding, Furniture move & cleanup

## Cities served (local context)
- Bradenton, FL (Manatee County) — https://bvaflooring.com/bradenton/ : 1950s concrete-block ranches near Palma Sola to newer waterfront builds along the Manatee River. Pricing tends a mid-market range, with slab-on-grade homes often needing leveling.
- Sarasota, FL (Sarasota County) — https://bvaflooring.com/sarasota/ : West-of-Trail estates, historic downtown bungalows, and key condos. Pricing tends toward the upper end, where premium materials and detailed layouts are common.
- Lakewood Ranch, FL (Manatee &amp; Sarasota Counties) — https://bvaflooring.com/lakewood-ranch/ : newer master-planned and golf-course homes in communities like Lakewood National and Waterside. Pricing tends at a premium, and HOA design rules often dictate product and color.
- Palmetto, FL (Manatee County) — https://bvaflooring.com/palmetto/ : older riverfront cottages and new builds north of the Manatee. Pricing tends value-focused, with budget LVP and laminate popular.
- Parrish, FL (Manatee County) — https://bvaflooring.com/parrish/ : fast-growing master-planned subdivisions like North River Ranch. Pricing tends new-construction value, with builder-grade upgrades common.
- Venice, FL (Sarasota County) — https://bvaflooring.com/venice/ : island bungalows and 55+ communities. Pricing tends mid-to-premium, with retiree-friendly, low-maintenance picks leading.
- Tampa, FL (Hillsborough County) — https://bvaflooring.com/tampa/ : South Tampa bungalows, Hyde Park historics, and new downtown condos. Pricing tends at an urban premium, with older pier-and-beam homes needing extra prep.
- St. Petersburg, FL (Pinellas County) — https://bvaflooring.com/st-petersburg/ : Old Northeast historic homes, Kenwood bungalows, and downtown condos. Pricing tends at a renovation premium, especially in protected historic districts.

## Common questions
Q: How do I get a flooring estimate from BVA Flooring?
A: Call, text, or WhatsApp (941) 807-0339, or fill out our online form. We schedule a free in-home measurement and send a written, itemized estimate within 24 hours — no obligation.
Q: What areas do you serve?
A: Bradenton, Sarasota, Lakewood Ranch, Palmetto, Parrish, Venice, Tampa, and St. Petersburg, FL — across Manatee, Sarasota, Hillsborough, and Pinellas counties on the Gulf Coast.
Q: Are you licensed and insured?
A: Yes. BVA Services Corp is a licensed and insured flooring installer. You deal directly with the crew that installs your floor — never a call center or a rotating subcontractor.
Q: How much does flooring installation cost in Tampa Bay?
A: As a 2026 guide: luxury vinyl plank runs about $5–$9/sq ft installed, laminate $4.50–$8.50, hardwood $9–$18, porcelain tile $9–$20, and stair treads $80–$240 per step. Your real number depends on the product and how much subfloor prep your home needs.
Q: Why won't you give an exact price over the phone?
A: Because an honest price needs a measurement. Square footage, subfloor condition, tear-out, and layout all move the number. Anyone quoting an exact total sight-unseen is guessing — we send a written, itemized estimate after a free measurement instead.
Q: How does payment work?
A: Typically a deposit at signing to reserve your install date and order materials, with the balance due when the job passes our final 52-point inspection. Everything is in writing up front — no surprise upcharges mid-job.
Q: What flooring is best for Florida humidity?
A: For most Gulf-Coast homes, waterproof luxury vinyl plank and engineered hardwood handle humidity best, with porcelain tile ideal for wet areas like bathrooms and lanais. We help you match the right product to each room — free.
Q: Should I choose vinyl plank, tile, or hardwood?
A: Vinyl plank is waterproof, warm, and great almost everywhere — especially rentals and busy homes. Tile is the most durable and best for wet areas. Engineered hardwood adds warmth and resale value in dry living spaces. Many Florida homes use a smart mix.
Q: Can you install over my existing floor?
A: Often yes. Rigid-core vinyl plank can sometimes float over sound, flat tile or hard flooring, saving tear-out cost. We'll tell you honestly after measuring whether that's a good idea in your home.
Q: How long does flooring installation take?
A: A room or two is usually 1–2 days; whole-home jobs take longer, especially if the subfloor needs leveling or tear-out. You get a firm timeline with your written estimate.
Q: Do you move furniture and remove the old floor?
A: Yes. We can handle furniture moving, tear-out, and haul-away of your old floor — listed as line items in your estimate so you know exactly what's included.
Q: What is the BVA 52-Point Floor-Ready Standard?
A: It's our documented, 52-point quality checklist covering site assessment, moisture testing, subfloor prep, acclimation, installation, and final inspection. Every floor passes it before we call the job done.
Q: Do you do moisture testing?
A: Always. Even waterproof flooring sits on a subfloor that can hold or transmit moisture. Documented moisture testing and a 48–72 hour acclimation window are standard on every BVA install — it's how we prevent mold, cupping, and adhesive failure.
Q: What warranty do you offer?
A: Every install comes with a written workmanship warranty, on top of the manufacturer's product warranty (which ranges from about 15 years to lifetime depending on the material). See our warranty page for details.
Q: Do you handle water-damage or insurance work?
A: Yes. We repair and replace water-damaged flooring and can document scope and photos to support an insurance claim. Start with our floor-repair service for a diagnostic visit.
Q: What happens if something goes wrong after installation?
A: Call us. As a local, owner-operated company, the same team that installed your floor handles any workmanship issue covered under your written warranty — no call center, no runaround.
